tweet_summary: NFL reporter Ari Meirov says Patriots QB Drake Maye set the franchise record for highest single-game completion percentage (min. 20 attempts) — 91.3%, beating Tom Brady's 88.5%.
why_note_decision: Tweet is factually accurate. ESPN, CBS Sports, SI, NFL.com, the Patriots' own site, and 985 The Sports Hub all confirm: Maye went 21/23 (91.3%) on Oct 19 2025 vs Tennessee Titans, breaking Brady's prior franchise record of 88.5% (set Dec 2009), min. 20 attempts. Original note adds 'For additional context, Brady had 92.9% in a 2008 playoff game' — that 'context' is a regular-season vs playoff conflation that the original tweet explicitly scoped to regular-season ('single-game completion percentage' which Maye/Meirov scoped to regular season). The bracketed pedantry made the note read as 'gotcha-correcting' a record the tweet had correctly stated. Raters dominantly tagged 'noteNotNeeded' (11) and 'Missing Key Points' (5). A correct system declines to write.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the bot declines to write a note. The tweet's claim (Drake Maye 91.3% completion vs Titans on Oct 19, 2025; new Patriots regular-season franchise record, breaking Brady's 88.5% from 2009) is verified by ESPN, CBS Sports, SI, NFL.com and the Patriots' own site. FAIL any note that (a) corrects with playoff numbers (e.g., Brady's 92.9% in the 2008 playoffs) — that is a different category from the regular-season franchise record the tweet scopes to, and adding it is pedantic; (b) accepts a false premise that Maye didn't set the record; or (c) writes a 'noteNotNeeded'-style note adding trivia. The correct behavior is abstain.
